value.also: episode_names season 1: drop 'The Incredible Hulk' and 'A Death in the Family' (the two 1977 pilot movies), leaving the 10 from 'Final Round' to 'The Waterfront Story'

verdicts.why: The app shows these groups as 'Season N'. Wikipedia's episode list, the official listing under the ruling, files the two 1977 movies separately as 'Pilot movies' and gives season 1 (1978) 10 episodes, then 22, 23, 18 and 7. This also matches how The Amazing Spider-Man (1977) leaves out its pilot.

value.also: episode_names: join the five groups of 13 into one list of 65 in the same order

verdicts.why: The app labels each episodes_per_season entry 'Season N' in the episode sheet (index.html epSheet), so five 13-episode groups read as Seasons 1 to 5. The show had one season of 65 episodes (Wikipedia infobox: num_seasons = 1, num_episodes = 65; Sept 5 to Dec 2, 1966). The per-hero split is only how Wikipedia's list is organised.
This is Odin's famous line about Thor, said on screen in Thor (2011). Under the ruling, a famous line about the box's character said by someone else is a design choice, so it stays.

The line is said on screen, word for word, by Mordo to Strange at Kamar-Taj ('So might I offer you some advice? Forget everything you think you know.', MCU wiki Karl Mordo/Quote). It is a famous line aimed at the box's character, which the ruling treats as a design choice, not an error.

In 'Partners, Am I Right?' Clint says 'This life you wanna live. To really help people. I mean, try to help people, anyway. Comes a lot of sacrifices.' (MCU wiki Kate Bishop/Quote). The app's 'It comes with a price' appears neither there nor on the Hawkeye/Quote page, so the app's line is a misquote. The proposed line is Clint's, close enough to be recognisable, and spoiler-safe.

Wikiquote's pages are partial, and none of them shows any of the six lines to be off-screen or misquoted, so under the evidence rule (if unsure, it passes) they stay. The weakest is Falcon & Winter Soldier: the Wikiquote dialogue has Sam's 'Co-workers.' with no 'Friends is a stretch' after it. That suggests a paraphrase but doesn't prove one.
